title: Spring vulnerability

indicators.comparison: 211 mm falls in November-April on average; 37% of the input springs get more.
indicators.why: Winter and pre-monsoon rain feeds the spring in the months it is lowest. Daniel 2021 rainfall stressor.

indicators.indicator: Built-up, cropland and bare land within 500 m
indicators.comparison: 2% of the land within 500 m is built-up, cropland or bare; 38% of the input springs have less.
indicators.why: Less forest and more sealed or tilled land means less infiltration near the spring. Stand-in until Module B maps the real recharge zone.

indicators.comparison: Yearly rain is 1.36 times the evaporation demand; 66% of the input springs are wetter.
indicators.why: Less water left over for recharge after evaporation.

indicators.comparison: Yearly rain changed by -0.5% per decade over 2001-2025 (IMD); 23% of the input springs are drying more slowly or getting wetter.
indicators.why: Falling rain means less recharge year after year: the rainfall stressor of Daniel et al. 2021. Trend over 25 IMD years (2001-2025); at most cells it is not statistically certain, so read it as a direction.

indicators.comparison: Yearly rain varies by 18% from year to year (IMD 2001-2025); 11% of the input springs vary less.
indicators.why: Dry years hit harder where rain swings a lot from year to year. 25 years of IMD data (2001-2025).

indicators.comparison: Mean slope within 500 m is 19 degrees; 16% of the input springs sit on gentler ground.
indicators.why: Steep slopes shed rain as runoff before it can soak in.

indicators.comparison: Buildings within 1 km changed by -5% from 2016 to 2023; 5% of the input springs saw less growth.
indicators.why: Stand-in for population growth: more houses mean more users and more sealed ground near the spring. Model estimates from yearly imagery, so small changes are noise.

indicators.indicator: Land rising above the spring within 1 km
indicators.comparison: The land rises 274 m above the spring within 1 km; 63% of the input springs have more land above them.
indicators.why: A spring close to a ridge top has little land above it to collect recharge.

context: Rock (GSI state map): Mixed (Carbonate, Phyllite, Shale): PHYLLITE, QTZ, SHALE,DOLOMITE, TUFF WITH DOLERITE (JAUNSAR)
Buildings within 1 km (Google Open Buildings): about 371 in 2016, 352 in 2023
Surface catchment above the spring (DEM): 8.3 ha. This is not the recharge area; Module B will estimate that.

rationale: Nobody has said yet whether the flow has fallen, so this is an exposure score: it shows how exposed the spring's setting is, not whether the spring is declining.
Rain / evaporation demand (aridity index) adds 8.2 points (scored 66/100): Yearly rain is 1.36 times the evaporation demand; 66% of the input springs are wetter.
Dry-season rain (Nov-Apr) adds 8.0 points (scored 37/100): 211 mm falls in November-April on average; 37% of the input springs get more.
Built-up, cropland and bare land within 500 m adds 5.9 points (scored 38/100): 2% of the land within 500 m is built-up, cropland or bare; 38% of the input springs have less.
